eyebrow: The speedup claim, apples to apples
code:
N = 2^n  (same transform, same size)

Classical FFT:   O(N log N) = O(n * 2^n) arithmetic ops
QFT circuit:     O(n^2) quantum gates
caption: O(n^2) vs. O(n * 2^n) is a real, undisputed exponential improvement in n — building the transform is exponentially cheaper, gate for gate.

steps.label: A classical FFT hands you all N output values
steps.sub: Print them, store them, feed them to the next stage — anything

steps.label: A quantum register can't be read out that way
steps.sub: One measurement collapses it to exactly one basis state

steps.label: Every other amplitude's information is gone
steps.sub: Rebuilding the full vector means re-running and re-measuring many times

steps.label: Done honestly, that erodes the gate-count advantage
steps.sub: The speedup isn't free once you need the full output

eyebrow: Not a flaw — a scoping condition

steps.label: Useful only when you don't need the full vector
steps.sub: When the surrounding algorithm needs one specific extractable fact

steps.label: Phase estimation: concentrates onto one basis state
steps.sub: Designed so a few measurements reveal one phase with high precision

steps.label: Shor's algorithm: needs only the period
steps.sub: The QFT step is engineered to peak on states that reveal it

steps.label: The speedup is real — and only accessible by design
